newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. body cancels NEC supercomputer purchase - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. body cancels NEC supercomputer purchase - paper.

text.p: The National Science Foundation (NSF), a U.S. governmental entity, has decided to cancel a planned purchase of NEC supercomputers, a major Japanese daily said on Sunday.

The Mainichi Shimbun said the decision was made by the University Corp of Atmospheric Research (UCAR), an NSF affiliate, in retaliation for NEC Corp's and its U.S. subsidiary, HNSX Supercomputers Inc's, request to suspend a Commerce Department anti-dumping investigation involving NEC supercomputers.

The investigation began after Cray Research Inc accused NEC of dumping or selling at deep discounts to achieve market share, and willing to take an estimated $65 million loss to supply supercomputing equipment to UCAR, a government-funded climate research centre in Colorado.
NEC said last Wednesday it planned to appeal if a U.S. federal court turned down its request.
The newspaper said UCAR sent NEC an unofficial notification of the decision, and that the company was already selling the supercomputers originally intended for NSF to another customer.
